newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up on Friday on short-covering, reversing the falls of the past two weeks, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended limit-up at 20,350 yuan ($2,454) per tonne, rising 600 yuan. It opened at 19,980 yuan and hit a low of 19,950 yuan per tonne.
August rose 450 to 20,100, September 640 to 20,260, October 610 to 20,350 and December 650 to 20,360 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 85,140 tonnes from 82,320 tonnes.
The contracts opened up but with most at intraday lows, rising further before closing at their limit-up.
Traders said overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME) had boosted the confidence of long position holders in Shanghai and many investors were eager to liquidate their short positions.
"Short-covering driven by heavy profits was responsible for day's sharp rise," one trader said.
"Long position holders did not want to offset because prices had not hit the levels at which they had bought," he added.

LME copper made steady upside afternoon progress on Thursday and ended firmly in the plus column after an early dip to five-month lows, with the benchmark three months metal ending at $2,280 per tonne, compared to $2,267 at Wednesday's finish.
Analysts in London said they expected LME copper to extend Thursday's spike higher, but players were nervous of a reversal around $2,300 a tonne, or at the next resistance level of $2,340/50.
LME copper stocks rose on Friday by 7,800 tonnes.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices recovered the 20,000-yuan level on the back of the futures rises, traders said.
But despite the day's rise, traders said the short-term market trend was still not optimistic.
"Investors were a little panicky today but they are likely to wake up on Monday," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected copper to meet strong resistance at high levels in the next few days.
Aluminium ended up. August rose 120 to 13,400 and September 200 to 13,400 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 230 tonnes from 5,600 tonnes.
